title: 03_VLM_Enrichment — Visual Content Enrichment
text:
Enrich extracted facts with visual context (charts, diagrams, flowcharts, tables, images) using VLMs, ensuring complete information capture from non-textual document elements.







Repo: github.com/docling-project/docling-graph
Developed by: Docling Team (IBM Research)
License: MIT
Models: Any backend (Ollama, vLLM, OpenAI, Anthropic, Mistral)
Use case: Schema-driven extraction from any document
Output: Pydantic → NetworkX (nodes + edges + provenance)
Key feature: Deterministic data grounding (no extra LLM calls)





Repo: github.com/sujiths/diagram2graph
Developed by: Sujith S (community)
License: Apache 2.0
Model: Fine-tuned Qwen2.5-VL-3B (PEFT/LoRA)
Benchmarks: Node F1 +14.2% (89.1%), Edge F1 +23.4% (69.45%)
Use case: Technical diagrams, architecture diagrams, flowcharts
Output: Neo4j-compatible JSON (nodes + edges)





Repo: github.com/FairmeHIT/Multi-VIE
Developed by: Huafu Li, Guo Chen, Jia Xia, et al. (HIT)
License: MIT (code); Apache 2.0 (model)
Model: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-SFT
Benchmarks: 93.65% F1 on multi-type extraction (16 certificate types)
Use case: Forms, invoices, contracts, certificates, official documents
Output: Structured JSON with type-specific landmarks





Repo: github.com/Wings-Of-Disaster/VaLiK
Developed by: Junming Liu, Siyuan Meng, et al. (ICCV 2025)
License: MIT
Method: Chain-of-Experts VLM pipeline
Use case: Annotation-free MMKG construction from images
Output: Direct entity-to-image linkage, knowledge graph





Repo: github.com/openbmb/visrag
Developed by: OpenBMB / Tsinghua University
License: Apache 2.0
Model: VisRAG-Ret (VLM-based retriever)
Use case: Direct image embedding (bypass OCR loss)
Benchmarks: 20-40% end-to-end improvement vs text-based RAG

       │
       ├── [Text-only regions] ──► Skip (already text-extracted)
       │
       ├── [Tables detected] ──► Docling table structure model
       │                          └──► Table cells → KG facts
       │
       ├── [Charts/graphs detected] ──► Qwen2.5-VL-7B caption
       │                               └──► Caption → NER → facts
       │
       ├── [Flowcharts/diagrams] ──► Diagram2Graph (fine-tuned VLM)
       │                              └──► Nodes + edges → KG

       │                            └──► Landmarks → KG facts
       │
       └── [Images without OCR text] ──► Multi-VIE / GPT-4o Vision

Should VLM run synchronously during intake (slows pipeline) or async background?
For diagrams, should we accept Diagram2Graph output directly, or re-verify with a second VLM?
What’s the confidence threshold to reject VLM extractions (currently proposed: 0.7)?
Should we VLM-enrich every image, or only those with no accessible alt-text?

Incremental VLM updates — No paper covers re-enriching changed images during incremental intake.

Proposed workaround: Compare image hashes; re-run VLM only if changed.

Cross-modal conflict resolution — When image-extracted fact conflicts with text-extracted fact.

Proposed workaround: Use recency + confidence + authority scoring (context-graph’s composite score).

Multi-language document support — Most extraction papers focus on English.

Proposed: Use multilingual VLM (Gemini 1.5 Pro) + language detection.

Audio/video temporal alignment — Aligning transcript timestamps with KG fact valid_at.

Proposed: Use Whisper word-level timestamps; store segment_start/segment_end metadata.

ZIP bomb safety — Limited academic work; engineering-only concern.

Proposed: Use AI-KE’s archive-bomb limits (max ratio 100:1, max 500MB).

Should we extend Docs2KG’s dual-path with our own VLM, or use Docling-Graph’s VLM directly?
Do we need a custom benchmark for samples5/ (domain-specific)? Suggested: derive from Docs2KG’s evaluation (multi-metric: textual accuracy + reading order).
Should the temporal validity of audio/video extractions use created_at from metadata (when file was created), or system ingested_at? Recommend: hybrid (use metadata if available, fallback to ingest time, flag confidence).
Is there a paper that covers incremental KG updates with VLM re-enrichment? Currently none found — may need custom solution (hash-based image change detection).
Should we produce a paper ourselves summarizing this assembly? Strong candidate for academic publication (e.g., system demonstration at ACL/ICLR).

        with self.driver.session() as sess:
            res = sess.run(
                "MATCH (f:Fact) WHERE f.entity_id=$e AND f.predicate=$p AND f.current=true "
                "RETURN f ORDER BY f.valid_at DESC", e=entity_id, p=predicate)
            return [dict(r["f"]) for r in res]

    def upsert_fact(self, fact_id, entity_id, predicate, object_value, as_of, source_file,
                    extraction_path, model_used, current=True, confidence=1.0):
        with self.driver.session() as sess:
            sess.run("""
                MERGE (f:Fact {fact_id:$fid})
                SET f.entity_id=$e, f.predicate=$p, f.object_value=$o,
                    f.valid_at=$a, f.source_file=$sf, f.extraction_path=$ep,
                    f.model_used=$m, f.current=$c, f.confidence=$conf,
                    f.created_at=datetime()
                """,
                fid=fact_id, e=entity_id, p=predicate, o=object_value, a=as_of.isoformat(),
                sf=source_file, ep=extraction_path, m=model_used, c=current, conf=confidence)

    def supersede(self, old_fact_id, new_fact_id, at_iso):
        with self.driver.session() as sess:
            sess.run("""
                MATCH (o:Fact {fact_id:$o}) MATCH (n:Fact {fact_id:$n})
                SET o.current=false, o.invalid_at=datetime($at), o.expired_at=datetime(),
                    o.superseded_by=$n

from datetime import datetime
from src.models import ReconciliationResult

def reconcile(new_fact, existing_facts: list) -> ReconciliationResult:
    """Most-recent-wins. Synchronous."""
    # Compare by entity_id + predicate. If newer valid_at => supersede.
    for old in existing_facts:
        if old["entity_id"] == new_fact["entity_id"] and old["predicate"] == new_fact["predicate"]:
            new_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(new_fact["valid_at"].replace("Z","+00:00"))
            old_dt = datetime.fromisoformat(old["valid_at"].replace("Z","+00:00"))
            if new_dt > old_dt:
                return ReconciliationResult(action="supersede",
                    superseded_fact_id=old["fact_id"],
                    reason=f"newer valid_at {new_dt} > {old_dt}")
    return ReconciliationResult(action="keep", reason="no conflict or not newer")



import json, hashlib, datetime
from pathlib import Path

class AuditLogger:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._prev_hash = self._last_hash()

    def _last_hash(self):
        if not self.path.exists(): return "GENESIS"
        last = self.path.read_text().strip().splitlines()[-1]
        return json.loads(last)["hash"]

    def log(self, event: dict):
        entry = {**event, "ts": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                 "prev_hash": self._prev_hash}
        h = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()

from neo4j import GraphDatabase
from src.config import get_settings

class TemporalKG:
    def __init__(self, uri=None, user=None, password=None):
        s = get_settings()
        self.driver = GraphDatabase.driver(
            uri or s.neo4j_uri,
            auth=(user or s.neo4j_user, password or s.neo4j_password),
        )

    def close(self):
        self.driver.close()

    def get_current_facts(self, entity_id, predicate):
        with self.driver.session() as sess:
            res = sess.run(
                "MATCH (f:Fact) WHERE f.entity_id=$e AND f.predicate=$p AND f.current=true "
                "RETURN f ORDER BY f.valid_at DESC", e=entity_id, p=predicate)
            return [dict(r["f"]) for r in res]

    def upsert_fact(self, fact_id, entity_id, predicate, object_value, as_of, source_file,
                    extraction_path, model_used, current=True, confidence=1.0):
        with self.driver.session() as sess:
            sess.run("""
                MERGE (f:Fact {fact_id:$fid})
                SET f.entity_id=$e, f.predicate=$p, f.object_value=$o,
                    f.valid_at=$a, f.source_file=$sf, f.extraction_path=$ep,
                    f.model_used=$m, f.current=$c, f.confidence=$conf,
                    f.created_at=datetime()
                """,
                fid=fact_id, e=entity_id, p=predicate, o=object_value, a=as_of.isoformat(),
                sf=source_file, ep=extraction_path, m=model_used, c=current, conf=confidence)

    def supersede(self, old_fact_id, new_fact_id, at_iso):
        with self.driver.session() as sess:
            sess.run("""
                MATCH (o:Fact {fact_id:$o}) MATCH (n:Fact {fact_id:$n})
                SET o.current=false, o.invalid_at=datetime($at), o.expired_at=datetime(),
                    o.superseded_by=$n
                MERGE (n)-[:SUPERSEDES]->(o)
            """, o=old_fact_id, n=new_fact_id, at=at_iso)

import json, hashlib, datetime
from pathlib import Path

class AuditLogger:
    def __init__(self, path):
        self.path = Path(path)
        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        self._prev_hash = self._last_hash()

    def _last_hash(self):
        if not self.path.exists(): return "GENESIS"
        last = self.path.read_text().strip().splitlines()[-1]
        return json.loads(last)["hash"]

    def log(self, event: dict):
        entry = {**event, "ts": datetime.datetime.now(datetime.timezone.utc).isoformat(),
                 "prev_hash": self._prev_hash}
        h = hashlib.sha256(json.dumps(entry, sort_keys=True).encode()).hexdigest()
        entry["hash"] = h
        with self.path.open("a") as f:
            f.write(json.dumps(entry) + "\n")
        self._prev_hash = h
        return h

Primary: Docs2KG (dual-path: programmatic parser + Doc Layout Analysis)
Secondary: Docling (layout-preserving, complex tables)
Tertiary: Semantica (broad format support)
Quaternary: AI-KE (audio/video/multimedia)









Method: Library-based parsers (PDFMiner, python-docx, openpyxl)
Libraries: PyMuPDF, pdfplumber, python-docx, openpyxl
Output: Raw text with position metadata (page, bbox)
Performance: ~100 pages/sec





Method: Tesseract 5.x / Tesseract LSTM / EasyOCR / PaddleOCR
Use Case: Scanned documents, image-based PDFs
Output: Text with confidence scores + bounding boxes
Performance: ~10 pages/sec





Method: CV-based layout detection (DocLayout, CNN-based)
Use Case: Multi-column, complex layouts
Output: Structured regions (title, paragraph, table, figure)
Performance: ~20 pages/sec





Method: Qwen2.5-VL-7B / GPT-4o Vision / Docling-Graph
Use Case: Diagrams, complex tables, charts
Output: Structured data + KG triples
Performance: ~2-5 pages/sec (model-bound)





Method: Direct XLSX/CSV → Neo4j Table nodes (AI-KE)
Use Case: Spreadsheets, database exports
Output: Table + Row nodes with properties
Performance: ~1000 rows/sec






Every extraction produces a normalized artifact:
{
  "doc_id": "uuid",
  "source_path": "samples5/report.pdf",
  "timestamp": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "as_of": "2024-01-15T10:30:00Z",
  "extraction_path": "text|ocr|layout|vlm|tabular",
  "model_used": "pymupdf|tesseract|qwen2.5-vl-7b",
  "chunks": [
    {
      "chunk_id": "uuid",
      "text": "CEO is Satya Nadella",
      "bbox": [x, y, w, h],
      "page": 1,
      "confidence": 0.98
    }
  ],
  "entities": [...],
  "relations": [...]
}
This feeds directly into Graphiti for reconstruction.











Risk
Mitigation




OCR quality on scanned docs
Use best OCR (Tesseract 5 LSTM) + confidence threshold (0.8)


Table cell recognition errors
Use Docling’s table structure model (92% accuracy)


Audio transcription noise
Whisper large-v3 + NLP post-processing


Video key-frame selection
Compute scene-change detection (SSIM threshold)


ZIP bomb / malicious archives
AI-KE’s archive-bomb limits (max size, ratio)


PDF stream decompression failures
Fallback from Docling → PyMuPDF → pdfminer


<
end








Should audio/video transcription happen offline (batch) or on-demand?
Max file size limit for intake (currently proposed: 500MB)?
Should ZIP extraction be automatic or manual approval?
Which OCR engine priority (Tesseract vs EasyOCR vs PaddleOCR)?
Should video frame extraction be at fixed intervals or scene-change?

Rationale (Military): Mature, ACID, transactional, well-tooled, supports bitemporal queries via properties, rich Cypher ecosystem, on-prem deployable. FalkorDB faster but less ecosystem; Memgraph similar with low edge. Neo4j favored for audit tooling and Cypher queryability by analysts.



Rationale: Rust-based, fast, supports payload filters (current=true), on-prem docker deploy, HNSW index, named collections. Lower memory than Weaviate; Chroma is single-node only.




LLM provider: OpenAI-compatible via internal gateway (gpt-4-turbo text, gpt-4o vision)
VLM: cloud GPT-4o / Gemini via gateway, fallback Qwen2.5-VL-7B-SFT on-prem





Graphiti provides episodes + hybrid retrieval + provenance.
RAGBrain provides supersession logic + checked generation + system-time replay.








:Document (file-level)
:Episode (ingestion event; Graphiti native)
:Entity (normalized person/org/place/concept)
:Fact (atomic extracted knowledge; carries temporal + provenance)
:Audit (audit records; immutable)





(Document)-[:HAS_EPISODE]->(Episode)
(Episode)-[:YIELDS]->(Entity) (provenance)
(Entity)-[:HAS_FACT {relation}]->(Entity) (with temporal props)
(Fact)-[:SUPERSEDES {at: timestamp}]->(Fact)
(Fact)-[:PROVENANCE {source, extraction_path, model, as_of}]->(Fact) (optional; folded into node props instead for simplicity)




fact_id        UUID
content        str
entity_id      UUID    # canonical identity
predicate      str     # e.g. "CEO_OF", "WORKS_AT"
valid_at       timestamp
invalid_at     timestamp (null if current)
created_at     timestamp
expired_at     timestamp (null if current)
source_file    str
extraction_path str    # text/ocr/vlm/table/audio/video
model_used     str
current        bool
confidence     float
embedding_id   str     # Qdrant point id
superseded_by  UUID (null if current)



CREATE CONSTRAINT ON (e:Entity) ASSERT e.entity_id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE CONSTRAINT ON (f:Fact) ASSERT f.fact_id IS UNIQUE;
CREATE INDEX ON :Fact(current);
CREATE INDEX ON :Fact(valid_at);
CREATE INDEX ON :Fact(invalid_at);
CREATE INDEX ON :Fact(entity_id);
CREATE INDEX ON :Fact(predicate);
CREATE INDEX ON :Document(source_path, valid_at);



Default (current):
MATCH (f:Fact {entity_id:$id, predicate:$pred})
WHERE f.current = true
RETURN f ORDER BY f.valid_at DESC
Historical as_of:
MATCH (f:Fact {entity_id:$id, predicate:$pred})
WHERE f.valid_at <= $as_of AND (f.invalid_at IS NULL OR f.invalid_at > $as_of)
RETURN f ORDER BY f.valid_at DESC
Supersession chain:
MATCH p=(f:Fact {fact_id:$id})-[:SUPERSEDES*]->(older)
RETURN p








Vector dimension: 768 (all-mpnet-base-v2)
Distance: Cosine
Payload filterable fields:

fact_id (keyword, unique)
entity_id (keyword)
predicate (keyword)
current (bool, indexed)
as_of (datetime, range filter)
source_file (keyword)
extraction_path (keyword)
model_used (keyword)
confidence (float)
content (text, payload only)





create_payload_index("current", type=bool)
create_payload_index("as_of", type=datetime)
create_payload_index("entity_id", type=keyword)



# Pure RAG (current only)
qdrant.search(collection, query_vector, filter=Filter(must=[FieldCondition("current", match=True)]), limit=K)

# RAG + historical
qdrant.search(..., filter=Filter(must=[FieldCondition("as_of", range=Range(lte=as_of))]))

data/
├── sqlite_jobs.db         # intake queue
├── neo4j/                 # data directory (dbms)
├── qdrant/                # storage directory
├── audit.jsonl            # append-only audit
└── snapshots/             # (optional) Semantica weekly snapshots

text:
This directory contains the technical design, planning artifacts, and implementation plan for the Temporal-Valid Knowledge Graph RAG System, assembled from the UPDATED_MODEL/ research and tailored specifically for a military document intelligence environment.
Military constraints assumed throughout: - Air-gapped / offline capability is mandatory (no cloud-only dependencies at runtime) - All decisions favor low-latency, auditable, deterministic pipelines - Data is classified; provenance, timestamps, and audit trails are load-bearing - Documents share similar formats (field manuals, after-action reports, IFF/SOP, readiness reports, equipment logs, comms transcripts) - External APIs (OpenAI) are only acceptable behind an internal gateway with redaction gate; nothing leaves the enclave

text:
Each row: Question → Decision → Military Rationale.










Question
Decision
Rationale




Graph backend: Neo4j/FalkorDB/Memgraph?
Neo4j
Mature, ACID, Cypher queryable by analysts, audit tooling; on-prem


Vector store: Qdrant/Weaviate/Chroma?
Qdrant
Rust, low memory, payload filters, on-prem docker


LLM provider: OpenAI
Confirmed — internal gateway
Military air-gap: gate behind internal LLM gateway; no keys in repo; redact gate


VLM: cloud GPT-4o/Gemini
Confirmed — primary VLM via gateway; fallback Qwen2.5-VL-7B-SFT on-prem
Cloud better accuracy; on-prem fallback for air-gap


Primary temporal engine: Graphiti + RAGBrain
Confirmed
Combined stack: episodes + supersession + checked generation














Question
Decision
Rationale




Audio/video: Online vs offline batch?
Offline batch (priority: offline)
Military docs with audio/vehicle logs must be air-gapped safe


ZIP archives: Auto-extract vs manual?
Auto-extract, depth ≤3, size caps
Document bundles are commonly zipped field packets; auto-intake needed


OCR priority: Tesseract/EasyOCR/PaddleOCR?
Tesseract (PaddleOCR secondary)
Tesseract offline installable (system pkg); Paddle better accuracy but heavier deps


Video frame extraction: 1fps vs scene-change?
Scene-change (SSIM threshold 0.3)
Military video (CCTV/UAV) has long static periods; scene-change saves compute


PDF threshold
80 chars (per spec)
Proven heuristic; military text dense enough














Question
Decision
Rationale




Reuse/Improve extract.py
Improve + reuse (add audio/video MOD dates; reuse mtime)
Timestamp is temporal authority; must handle more formats


Supersession: sync vs background?
Synchronous
Classified data must resolve conflicts immediately, not eventual


Snapshots: per-ingest vs weekly?
Per-ingest + weekly prune (keep last 52)
Audit trail mandatory; per-ingest via Semantica TemporalVersionManager


Entity resolution: Semantica vs Graphiti?
Both: Semantica ML fuzzy first, then Graphiti LLM canonical
Military similar docs benefit from robust dedup; two-pass














Question
Decision
Rationale




Reranking: ms-marco vs LLM-as-reranker?
ms-marco-MiniLM (fast) + LLM-as-reranker for top-20 (optional flag)
Default fast; critical queries opt into slower LLM


Query cache: enable 1-hr TTL?
DISABLE query cache by default
Classified queries should not be retained; manual enable per scope


as_of detection: expose vs auto-detect?
Expose (explicit as_of param)
Military auditors need explicit control; auto-detect ambiguous


Checked generation: always vs Mode 2?
Always in Mode 2; Mode 3 configurable; Mode 1 never (speed)
Critical intelligence must be verified







Should classified PII redaction happen at intake or at query-time? Recommend: intake-time.
Should samples5/ be polled vs OS-event? Recommend: OS event (inotify); poll fallback.
Should there be multi-tenancy (org_unit scoping) from day 1? Recommend: yes, org_unit in schema to avoid re-migration.
Are audio/video transcripts considered classified? Assume yes; treat like text.
Should export allow only the user’s org data? Recommend: yes, enforce via query filter.

  → Graphiti.add_episode(content, source, valid_at, valid_at, metadata)
  → Conflict detection (entity id + predicate match)

  → Create AUDIT node
  → Create vectors in Qdrant (current=true metadata)
  → Hierarchical indexing (HiRAG community summaries)

title: UPDATED_MODEL — System Overview
text:
This directory contains the planning and assembly artifacts for the upgraded Temporal-Valid Knowledge Graph RAG System with Multi-Path Extraction, as defined in 01_Proposal.md.
The goal is to take a very basic RAG model and, by combining existing, production-grade open-source Git projects, evolve it into an advanced system that supports:

Flexible document intake (PDF, Excel, Word, audio, video, archives, images)
VLM enrichment (charts, diagrams, tables, OCR)
Temporal reconstruction (bi-temporal KG, supersession, provenance)
Hierarchical indexing (layered KGs)
Hybrid retrieval (Pure RAG / RAG+KG / KG-only, all temporal-aware)


No core algorithm is rewritten. Existing projects are wired together through configuration and thin adapter code (~200 lines max).





Don't rebuild. Assemble. Wire. Configure. Ship.
Every subsystem in this plan is mapped to a specific Git project or library that already implements it in production. The engineering effort is in:

Integrating via APIs
Configuring for the samples5/ directory
Adapting output schemas
Testing the combined pipeline

    valid_at: str  # ISO-8601 UTC
    ingest_method: str  # text|ocr|table|vlm|audio|video|archive
    text: str
    entities: list[dict] = Field(default_factory=list)
    relations: list[dict] = Field(default_factory=list)
    metadata: dict = Field(default_factory=dict)
    model_used: str = "docling"
    confidence: float = 1.0

class Fact(BaseModel):
    fact_id: str = Field(default_factory=lambda: str(uuid.uuid4()))
    content: str
    entity_id: str
    predicate: str

    valid_at: str
    invalid_at: Optional[str] = None
    created_at: str
    expired_at: Optional[str] = None
    source_file: str
    extraction_path: str
    model_used: str
    current: bool = True
    confidence: float = 1.0
    embedding_id: Optional[str] = None
    superseded_by: Optional[str] = None

class RetrievedFact(BaseModel):
    fact_id: str
    content: str
    source: str
    as_of: str
    current: bool
    confidence: float
    citation: str
    extraction_path: Optional[str] = None
    model_used: Optional[str] = None

class AnswerResponse(BaseModel):
    answer: str
    facts: list[RetrievedFact]
    mode: ModeType
    confidence: float = 0.0
    audit_id: str
    supported_claims: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)
    unsupported_claims: list[str] = Field(default_factory=list)

    include_history: bool = False
    org_unit: Optional[str] = None
    k: int = 10

title: 04_Reconstruction — Temporal KG Construction & Conflict Resolution
text:
Convert extracted entities/facts into a temporal knowledge graph with:

As-of timestamps (from file metadata via reuse of extract.py)
Provenance (source, extraction path, model)
Conflict detection (entity identity + provenance)
Supersession (most-recent-wins, retain history)
Audit trails








Repo: github.com/getzep/graphiti
Developed by: Zep Inc.
License: Apache 2.0
Stars: 32K
Key features:

Temporal fact management (validity windows)
Episodes & provenance (full lineage)
Incremental construction (no batch rebuild)
Hybrid retrieval (vector + KG + BM25)
Hyperparameter-tuned entity/relation extraction
Multiple backends: Neo4j, FalkorDB, Memgraph
Bi-temporal support (also provides transaction time)

Why chosen: Most mature; production-tested; supports all three retrieval modes





Repo: github.com/Nagendhra-Madishetti/ragbrain
Developed by: Nagendhra Madishetti
License: Apache 2.0
Key features:

Bi-temporal model (4 timestamps per fact)
superseded_by back-links at write time
System-time replay (audit)
Checked generation (claim-by-claim verification)
Pluggable everything (embedder, reranker, backend)
Multi-replica ready (shared session state)

Why chosen: Explicit conflict resolution; citation-ready answers





Repo: github.com/semantica-agi/semantica
License: MIT
Key features: GraphBuilder(merge_entities=True); fuzzy/exact/ML-based resolution
Use case: Deduplicate entities before KG insertion (e.g., “Apple”, “Apple Inc.”, “AAPL”)





Repo: github.com/kborovik/zeit
License: Proprietary (zeit-graph on PyPI)
Key features: Bi-temporal clocks, expires old fact, history retained
Use case: Fallback if Graphiti alone insufficient





Repo: github.com/williebsweet/context-graph
License: (check)
Key features: 4 conflict types; 4 resolution strategies; recency wins
Use case: Reference implementation for conflict detection taxonomy






Entity/Relation Extracts (from Intake)
       │
       ├── [1] Entity Resolution (Semantica)
       │       merge_entities=True → dedup "Apple"/"AAPL"/"Apple Inc."
       │
       ├── [2] Temporal Metadata Attachment (reuse extract.py)
       │       file mtime → valid_at (as-of timestamp)
       │       source file, extraction path, model → provenance
       │
       ├── [3] Graphiti Episode Creation
       │       graphiti.add_episode(
       │         content=fact,
       │         source=...,
       │         timestamp=as_of,
       │         valid_at=as_of,
       │         metadata={provenance}
       │       )
       │
       ├── [4] Conflict Detection (Graphiti + RAGBrain)
       │       • Identify matching entity identity
       │       • Compare as-of timestamps
       │       • If newer: mark older superseded
       │       • Create superseded_by edge
       │
       └── [5] Audit + Versioning
               • Retain old facts (current=false)
               • Record mutation history
               • Create snapshot (optional, via Semantica TemporalVersionManager)




Every fact MUST carry:



Field
Source




valid_at
File mtime (from extract.py)


invalid_at
Set when superseded


created_at
System time of ingest


expired_at
Set when superseded (system time)


source_file
Path to document


extraction_path
text / ocr / vlm / table / …


model_used
Name + version


current
Boolean flag


superseded_by
UUID of newer fact







On ingest new fact F_new:
  FOR each existing fact F_old WHERE:
    entity_id(F_new) == entity_id(F_old) AND
    predicate(F_new) == predicate(F_old):
      IF valid_at(F_new) > valid_at(F_old):
          # Conflict: promote new, demote old
          F_new.current = true
          F_old.current = false
          F_old.invalid_at = valid_at(F_new) - epsilon
          F_old.expired_at = now()
          F_old.superseded_by = F_new.id
          CREATE EDGE F_new SUPERSEDES F_old
      ELSE:
          # Older new; mark current but don't promote
          F_new.current = false
          F_new.superseded_by = F_old.id (informative)

Default retrieval filter: current = true




Per the proposal, the existing extract.py provides file modification/edit timestamps. To reuse:

Locate extract.py (currently exists in repo root)
Wrap it to produce valid_at timestamps for Graphiti episodes:
from extract import get_file_modified_time
valid_at = get_file_modified_time(source_path)
graphiti.add_episode(content, source_path, valid_at=valid_at)
Improve it if it only captures creation time (need modification time); expose both.




Should extract.py be improved (e.g., to handle audio/video creation dates)?
Or only reused as-is (and supplemented by other timestamp sources)?







Retain full history (do not delete old facts).
Use Semantica’s TemporalVersionManager (SQLite backend) for periodic graph snapshots (optional but recommended).
Provide query_history(entity_id) returning all facts (current + superseded) with timestamps and sources.
Use RAGBrain’s system-time replay to answer “what did the system know on date D?”












Risk
Mitigation




Entity ID mismatch across sources
Use hash-based canonical IDs (Semantica fuzzy merge)


Concurrent ingestion race conditions
Use transactional graph DB (Neo4j/FalkorDB ACID)


Supersession logic errors
Use Graphiti’s built-in invalidation + tests


Audit performance degradation
Periodic snapshot + archival (Semantica prune_versions)


Missing timestamps
Fallback to now() system time; flag as low confidence








Which graph DB backend (Neo4j vs FalkorDB vs Memgraph)?

Recommendation: FalkorDB (fast, in-memory, temporal graph natively).

Should KG snapshots be automatic (per ingest) or manual?
How to handle partial conflicts (only some relations change)?
Should invalidation be synchronous or via background queue?

All three retrieval modes must default to current=true facts:

Pure RAG — vector search over current facts
RAG + KG Validator — hybrid hits, KG overrides stale

Hybrid retrieval: vector + keyword + graph traversal
Temporal filtering via search query params
MultiHop traversal for complex questions
Pluggable vector backends

Provides all three retrieval modes natively





Repo: github.com/Nagendhra-Madishetti/ragbrain
Key features:

As-of retrieval (validity-filtered before ranking)
Checked generation: claim-by-claim verification
Citation-enriched answers
System-time replay for audit

Repo: Code at arxiv.org/abs/2025.findings-emnlp.321

License: MIT

Repo: github.com/jamjet-labs/engram
Key features:

HybridRetriever (vector + keyword + temporal)
Reader modes (recall vs synthesis)
Active fact versioning (supersede() filters old by default)

Use case: Mature hybrid retrieval with temporal scoring








INPUT: query
  1. Encode query → embedding
  2. Vector search top-K where metadata.current=true
     (metadata stored at ingestion time by Graphiti/RAGBrain)

Libraries: Graphiti.search(query, modes=[‘vector’]) Temporal filter: current=true metadata




INPUT: query
